title: Unit 6 · Daily routines
description: Reflexive verbs, telling time, everyday activities, frequency, and ordering a routine.
source: Original exercises aligned to the Aula Internacional Plus 1 Unit 6 syllabus; no textbook exercise text copied.

cards.note: Despertarse is reflexive and changes e to ie: me despierto.

cards.translation: What time do you wake up?
cards.note: The reflexive pronoun for tú is te.
Use se with the third-person form levanta.
The reflexive pronoun for nosotros is nos.

cards.translation: In the morning I take a shower.
cards.note: Ducharse is regular: me ducho.
Vestirse changes e to i: se viste.

cards.translation: I go to bed at eleven.
cards.note: Acostarse changes o to ue: me acuesto.

cards.translation: They go to bed late on Fridays.
cards.note: The ellos form is se acuestan.

cards.translation: Before eating, I wash my hands.
cards.note: Use the reflexive pronoun me with lavo.

cards.translation: After breakfast, I brush my teeth.
cards.note: Spanish uses the definite article los with body parts.
Sentirse changes e to ie: me siento.
Llamarse literally means to call oneself.
Use singular es with la una.
Use plural son with all hours except one.
Y cuarto means quarter past.
Y media means half past.
Menos cuarto means quarter to the next hour.
Use y plus the minutes after the hour.

cards.translation: What time does the class start?
cards.note: ¿A qué hora...? asks when an event happens.
Use a before a clock time.

cards.translation: I have breakfast in the morning.
cards.note: Por la mañana means in the morning.
Por la tarde means in the afternoon.
Por la noche means at night.

cards.prompt: Yo ___ café y pan por la mañana.
cards.translation: I have coffee and bread for breakfast in the morning.
cards.note: Desayunar means to have breakfast.
Comemos is the nosotros form of comer.

cards.translation: She works from nine to five.
cards.note: De nueve a cinco means from nine to five.
Volver changes o to ue: vuelvo.

cards.translation: Every day I make the bed.
cards.note: Hacer is irregular in the yo form: hago.

cards.translation: My parents have dinner at eight.
cards.note: Cenan is the ellos form of cenar.
Dormir changes o to ue: duermo.

cards.translation: I always have breakfast before working.
cards.note: Siempre means always.

cards.translation: I usually go to work by metro.
cards.note: Normalmente and generalmente both mean usually.
A veces means sometimes.

cards.translation: I never drink coffee at night.
cards.note: Nunca before the verb makes the sentence negative without no.
Todos los días means every day.

cards.prompt: Voy al gimnasio una vez a la ___.
cards.translation: I go to the gym once a week.
cards.note: Una vez a la semana means once a week.

cards.translation: First I shower; then I have breakfast.
cards.note: Primero introduces the first action in a sequence.
Después de is followed by a noun or infinitive.

cards.translation: Before sleeping, I read a little.
cards.note: Antes de is followed by a noun or infinitive.

cards.translation: I have dinner and then watch a series.
cards.note: Luego and después can both mean then.
Salir is irregular in the yo form: salgo.

cards.translation: I arrive at work at nine.
cards.note: Llegar is regular in the present tense.
